title: Uniqueness of normalized primitive quotient realizations
statement: Fix a prime l, finite coefficient extensions E,L and an embedding i:E -> L. Let f:X -> Y be any scheme map, S a whole-system reduction calculus on Y [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and rho_X,rho_L normalized Roos models. Any two IntegralComparisonPullbackModel structures for f,S,rho_X have equal natural realization isomorphisms. Any two IntegralComparisonScalarModel structures for i,Y,S,rho_L have equal natural realization isomorphisms. All models and their representative normalizations are exactly [def-trf-integral-comparison-realization-models]. Universes are independent and no constructibility assumption is imposed.

proof.text: For a good flat-term K-flat representative P obtain C,e,kappa together with both its finite-horizontal presentation equations and its whole-system adjunction coherence from coherentPrimitiveReductionPresentation. Apply both pullback normalizations to this same coherent presentation, supplying both proofs. Compare q and q-prime by the target endomorphism q-prime inverse followed by q. At level n and degree i, every target finite pullback unit generator is the image under both q and q-prime of the same source generator: choose its input using kappa inverse and the inverse identification of evaluation sections. The q-prime inverse identity then shows that this endomorphism fixes every target unit generator. The existing restricted pullback Hom extensionality theorem applies because the completed coefficient projection is locally surjective. Extensionality over chain degrees and strict tower levels gives q-prime inverse composed with q equal to the identity, hence q=q-prime. The two normalization equations now have exactly the same postcomparison. It is invertible since its composite with either realization is the prescribed pullback comparison isomorphism; cancel it to obtain equality at Q(P).

source.place: Tags 06YS, 06YY and 0941; parent proof step 6, uniqueness on representative-normalized primitive comparisons

proof.text: For scalar change choose a simultaneous whole-system coherent presentation from coherentPrimitiveReductionPresentation and apply both normalizations with this coherence proof to obtain the two normalized strict tower comparisons q,q-prime. Test q-prime inverse followed by q on every target balanced tensor generator s tensor x at each level and degree. The displayed scalar normalization formulas give one common source section, formed with kappa inverse and the finite scalar-unit tensor, that q and q-prime both carry to s tensor x. The inverse identity for q-prime therefore makes this endomorphism fix all these generators. Apply the existing integralScalarReduction_hom_ext theorem, which proves equality after sheafification by tensor induction, then chain and strict tower extensionality. Thus q=q-prime. The common postcomparison, including the universal cochain counit and normalized Roos factor, is invertible because either normalization equation identifies its composite with a realization isomorphism with the prescribed scalar comparison isomorphism. Cancel that postcomparison to identify the scalar realization components at Q(P).

proof.text: The existing good-complex localization theorem makes the good-representative localization essentially surjective. For each ambient derived object K choose a good representative P with an isomorphism Q(P) to K. Naturality of the two pullback realizations transports their equality at Q(P) to K by cancellation of the image of this isomorphism. Do the same for the scalar realizations. Natural-transformation and natural-isomorphism extensionality give the two asserted equalities. This uses no faithfulness of finite derived evaluations and imposes no constructibility, nonzero-input, or unequal-field hypothesis.

lean.statement:
theorem primitiveQuotientRealizations_unique
    {X Y : Scheme.{t}} (f : X ⟶ Y)
    (SY : CoefficientDerivedSystemCalculus l E Y)
    (ρX : IntegralComparisonRoosModel l E X)
    (ρL : IntegralComparisonRoosModel l L Y)
    (α : IntegralComparisonPullbackModel l E f SY ρX)
    (β : IntegralComparisonScalarModel l E L ι Y SY ρL) :
    (∀ α' : IntegralComparisonPullbackModel l E f SY ρX,
      α'.realization = α.realization) ∧
    (∀ β' : IntegralComparisonScalarModel l E L ι Y SY ρL,
      β'.realization = β.realization)
